clue.text: Two companies head for source of oil

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company, taken twice
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Two firms lead the hunt for a new oilfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of oil' sounds like a well or field, but it is a fruit pressed for its oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Coconut oil is pressed from the dried flesh of the palm's fruit, so the fruit is a source of it.

clue.text: Persuade with drinks, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the word goes by its sound

blocks.note: Cokes are fizzy drinks

explanation.surface: Win someone round by plying them with drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to persuade gently by flattery or patience, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Manage without special potential

indicators.note: being without something means lacking it, so it is removed

blocks.note: S is an abbreviation for special
scope for improvement is potential

explanation.surface: Getting by without any particular promise.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to manage or get by in difficult circumstances, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bird at northern university to fix the roof?

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
U is the abbreviation for university
to thatch is to cover a roof with straw, the question mark flagging the loose definition

explanation.surface: A bird at a northern university is asked whether it will repair the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small woodland bird that climbs tree trunks head-first, an example of the category.

clue.text: Small child not in bed to do addition

blocks.note: a tot is a toddler
someone up has got out of bed

explanation.surface: A toddler stays up past bedtime doing sums.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is to add numbers together to reach a total, a phrasal verb meaning sum.

clue.text: Outlook of snake prior to shock treatment

indicators.note: coming before something means this piece is placed first in the word

blocks.note: the asp is a small venomous snake
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A snake's mood before being given electric therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A house's outlook is the direction it faces, also called its aspect.

clue.text: Stiffener for celebrity before church

indicators.note: coming before places this piece at the front of the word

blocks.note: a star is a celebrity
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A famous person needs a stiff collar before attending a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is applied to fabric to make collars and shirts stiff, so it is a stiffening agent.

clue.text: With which to look at good girls?

definitions.text: With which to look at good girls?

blocks.note: to eye something is to look at it
G is the abbreviation for good
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about what a man uses for ogling attractive women.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, glasses being what one looks through, while its words also build it piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeglasses are lenses worn to improve sight, the means by which someone looks at anything.

clue.text: Hackneyed article about study by Rod

indicators.note: to go about something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the rest
standing by means next to, so these pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: the definite article
to read a subject is to study it
a bar is a rod

explanation.surface: A tired old piece of writing on a study by someone called Rod.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like a man's name, but it is a plain metal rod. 'About' here means surrounding, not concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare, literally worn thin, also describes an argument or joke so overused it has become stale.

clue.text: Cut off a partner pinching deposit

indicators.note: to pinch something is to grip it tightly, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a mate is a partner
to put something down is to deposit it

explanation.surface: Sever ties with a partner who steals the money you paid in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' reads as money in the bank; here it is the verb, to set something down.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons amputate a limb when they remove it entirely, a verb synonym for severing.

clue.text: Run rapidly from end of needle held by nurse

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
something held by another sits inside its grasp, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a carer looks after the sick, like a nurse
the final letter of the word needle

explanation.surface: Fleeing in panic from a needle's point held by a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along at speed, often out of control, a verb synonym for running fast.

clue.text: Secret not to keep in court?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
to lose something is the opposite of keeping it

explanation.surface: A confidential matter that should not be held back in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Closet as an adjective means hidden or secret, as in a closet fan, from the small private room.

clue.text: Take everything back after girl cops wine

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left
coming after places this piece at the end of the word

blocks.note: Val is a girl's name
cops are the police
everything is all

explanation.surface: The police take back all the wine a girl had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' only joins the parts; 'back' turns everything round, not the cops.
explanation.definitionFit: Valpolicella is a red wine made near Verona in northern Italy, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Stylish woman in English cathedral city

blocks.note: chic means stylish
Hester is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed woman visiting an English city with a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Chichester is the county town of West Sussex on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichester has a Norman cathedral and city status, an example of an English cathedral city.

clue.text: Bachelor's free to empty evening chamber for newly-wed

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only the outside letters

blocks.note: B for bachelor, as in a BA degree
to rid is to free
the first and last letters of the word evening
a room is a chamber

explanation.surface: A single man must clear out the evening's function room for a just-married couple.
explanation.walkthrough: Bachelor's misleads because it fits the wedding picture, but it only gives B; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridegroom is the man just married at a wedding, so he is a newly-wed.

clue.text: In race with Shed he's awful: tough luck!

indicators.note: something awful is a terrible mess, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner called Shed performs dreadfully in a race, and someone says bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of he's stands for 'is': the letters of race, Shed and he are awful. Hard cheese is a British, slightly mocking way of saying too bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cheese is a British idiom offering mock sympathy for someone's bad luck.

clue.text: English earl claims one in five offspring of the horse

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece grips another inside

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a quin is one of quintuplets, five children born together
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: An English nobleman claims one of his quintuplets is descended from a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: E and E together wrap round QUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine is the adjective from Latin equus, meaning relating to horses.

clue.text: Cry during cheerless obituary

indicators.note: something during an event happens within it, so the letters lie inside the words

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and first two of the second

explanation.surface: Weeping over a gloomy death notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To sob is to cry with convulsive breaths, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Carriage driver's train crew

blocks.note: to coach is to train
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: The driver of a carriage belongs to a railway crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Train and crew read as nouns from a railway, but both are verbs here; carriage is a horse-drawn coach, not a rail car.
explanation.definitionFit: A coachman drives a horse-drawn coach or carriage, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Fish part out of bulge in breeches?

indicators.note: taking something out of a word removes it, leaving the remainder

blocks.note: a piece is a part
the pouch at the front of old men's breeches

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about what is stuffed inside someone's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: A codpiece was the padded flap at the crotch of Tudor breeches; take PIECE away and a fish is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The cod is a large North Atlantic food fish, an example of the general category.

clue.text: Ace routine danced by hammer wielder

indicators.note: dancers move about the floor, so these letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A brilliant dance number performed by someone swinging a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: The hammer is not a tool but the gavel brought down to close a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer bangs a small gavel to mark each lot as sold, so wields a hammer.

clue.text: Animal caught mad cow disease somewhere else

indicators.note: something caught is trapped inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an ant is a creature
bovine spongiform encephalopathy, the medical name

explanation.surface: A farm animal has contracted mad cow disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Animal suggests the cow; it is the tiny ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means not present, so somewhere else, an adjective synonym used predicatively.

clue.text: Spurs lad with order for some food

blocks.note: to egg someone on is to spur them
Saint Benedict founded the Benedictine monastic order

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur, nicknamed Spurs, sign a youngster who orders a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs looks like the football club; it is the verb, to egg on. Benedict is a man's name whose saint gave his name to a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs Benedict is a dish of poached eggs and ham on a muffin with hollandaise, an example of food.

clue.text: Game moves quickly

blocks.note: first meaning: the pub game of throwing arrows at a board
second meaning: to dash or shoot forward suddenly

explanation.surface: A sport played at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a pub throwing game, and the verb means to dash suddenly in one direction.

clue.text: Game reserve

blocks.note: first meaning: the cue sport played on a table
second meaning: a shared stock of resources

explanation.walkthrough: Game reserve suggests a wildlife park; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a cue sport like billiards and also a common fund or supply held in reserve.

clue.text: Excess left in belly?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the gut is the belly
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Too much food stays in the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut is an oversupply, more than is needed, a noun synonym for surplus.

clue.text: Absorbent cloth covering king's tool

indicators.note: a covering goes round what it covers, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a towel soaks up water
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A towel draped over the king's gardening implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool for digging or spreading mortar.

clue.text: Odd context for odd series of musical beats

indicators.note: a context surrounds whatever sits within it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: droll means amusingly odd
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A puzzled musician remarks on a strange setting for a strange run of beats.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'odd's mean strange, one of them in the British slang sense, and 'context' says the first surrounds the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum roll is a rapid continuous succession of drumbeats, often used to build suspense.

clue.text: Meteor spinning far away

indicators.note: something spinning tumbles over and over, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A meteor tumbling through distant space.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote describes a place a long way off, an adjective synonym for distant.

clue.text: Garment produced by son at home with government permit

blocks.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
someone at home is in
G abbreviates government
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A vest made by a son working from home under a state licence.
explanation.walkthrough: A singlet is the British word for a sleeveless vest worn under a shirt or for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless undershirt or athletic vest, an example of a garment.
